The installation / the use / the operation of the optional plugins are in the README of each of them: `katana/README.md` · `health/README.md` · `notify/README.md`. **It is for the authorized scenarios only** (see the prerequisites and the compliance below). This tool **only collects information**, it does not exploit anything.

> **The plugins of the domestic registries**: `db_align` (the graph of the legal entities, it marks the LOCKED tag) and `ymicp` (the reverse lookup of the filing of the mini programs / of the WeChat accounts) read the Chinese corporate and the ICP registries, so they work only for the targets of China. Upgrading does not need a new `init`. Agents run the server through `npx`, so they pick up a new release the next time they start. If you moved to a fixed global install (see What leaves your machine), nothing updates until you install a newer version yourself. If `npx @make0-ai/brain --version` shows an old version, a global install is shadowing npx: `npm install -g @make0-ai/brain@latest`. On first open, a new version migrates `brain.db` in place, one transaction per step, so a failed step leaves the database as it was. Migrations add tables and columns and fill in new fields; they do not remove your memories. Older versions are not tested against a migrated database, so back up before upgrading if you might go back.

Each release is published to npm from GitHub Actions with provenance, tagged `vX.Y.Z` in GitHub Releases, and listed in the MCP Registry. CHANGELOG.md describes what changed. Patch releases are fixes. Minor releases can add features and database migrations.
